description: Forged-blueprint via symlink ingestion. ``cc/blueprints/`` is in write_guard's ``ALLOWED_PREFIXES_IN_PROTECTED`` so legitimate session-id-named JSON files can land there. Pre-fix, an attacker could create a symlink at ``cc/blueprints/latest.json`` pointing to attacker-controlled JSON outside the repo (e.g. ``/tmp/forged.json``) — write_guard had no ``ln -s`` extractor, so the symlink creation was allowed, and ``cognitive_blueprint._load_latest`` followed the symlink on the next session's load, ingesting forged session context that the operator saw as real ``LAST:`` continuation. Two-layer fix: (a) ``cognitive_blueprint._load_latest`` and ``cmd_chain`` per-file loop now refuse ``Path.is_symlink()`` files; (b) ``write_guard`` adds a dedicated ``check_bash_for_protected_symlinks`` that runs BEFORE the allowlist-aware general path check, blocking ``ln -s <target> <linkname>`` where linkname lands in any governed prefix (protected OR allowed-in-protected). Symlinks bypass the file-path allowlist by design — the allowlist exists for JSON FILE writes, not link entries.
